newsitem.title: UK: Thorn rebuffs press comment on Crazy George.
newsitem.headline: Thorn rebuffs press comment on Crazy George.

text.p: Thorn Plc described as "inaccurate" on Monday an article about its discount store chain Crazy George in the Mail on Sunday newspaper.

"Customers can buy for cash, on weekly terms with a 29.9 percent APR, or on weekly terms with a 29.9 percent APR and an optional service agreement. All this is absolutely clear to our customers," said the company in a statement.

The newspaper said Crazy George, which targets low earners and those on benefits, had been criticised for its "option service cover" offer which raised the interest rate on transactions to more than 80 percent from an advertised 29.9 percent.
The Office of Fair Trading confirmed that trading standards officers had raised concerns relating to Crazy George's but would not comment further, citing confidentiality.

In the statement Thorn said after a "very positive meeting with the Office of Fair Trading, we have no reason to believe that either our Authority Trading Standards or the Office of Fair Trading are unhappy with our contracts or trading policies."
Thorn shares, which went ex-dividend today, were 9-1/2 pence lower at 165p at 0950 GMT.
